text.tspan: 5′UTR reporter library with measured MRL
Goal: predict MRL for new sequences
Same kind of assay and scale?
Fixed leader, 50-nt insert, fixed CDS, polysome MRL,
about 70,000 labelled training records
Outside the tested scope
Run a grouped comparison on your own labels
Can you train a small CNN?
(one seed took 174–313 s on Apple MPS;
a full CPU-only run was not tested)
Cheap combined ridge
Grouped MSE 0.776, R² 0.643
20.7 s with features and alpha search, 0.45 GB
Will candidates share a parent sequence or an
identical 20-nt substring with training sequences?
One-hot CNN
Random split: MSE reduction +0.422 [+0.363, +0.488]
Main use: MRL values
or a top-1% pick list?
One-hot CNN
Grouped MSE 0.560 vs 0.776
No supported difference
CNN precision gain +0.020 [−0.088, +0.132]
Interval allows a gain of about 0.1 or a similar loss;
equality is not shown. Ridge is the cheaper option
Frozen UTR-LM input instead of one-hot:
no supported difference on the grouped split (−0.010 [−0.034, +0.016])
adds a 134.8 s CPU embedding pass and a 1.28 GB cache.
With a ridge head it was worse than cheap ridge
(grouped MSE reduction −0.244 per-position, −0.363 mean).
Random split, CNN head: MSE +0.021 (below threshold), P@150 −0.127
Before trusting any model:
check error by read-depth quartile and by sequence family;
run a CPU vs accelerator known-answer check
